nodes.purpose: Weighted A-star searches over terrain costs, hierarchical abstract graphs for long routes, and local searches for short routes.

cards.name: Fixed simulation timestep
cards.summary: OpenRA advances gameplay on a fixed timestep whose default is 40 milliseconds, which is 25 updates per second.
cards.behavior: The game-speed setting selects a timestep and an order latency. The Red Alert mod lists six profiles: 80, 50, 40, 35, 30 and 20 milliseconds per tick from slowest to fastest, and its default profile is the 40 millisecond one. The default profile runs a world tick every 40 milliseconds, so movement, reloads, and projectiles all resolve at 25 ticks per second. Order latency counts network frames, and one network frame spans 3 simulation ticks by default. In multiplayer the server applies the profile latency; the server field starts at 1 otherwise. Render frames do not drive simulation logic.

constants.name: Default timestep
constants.unit: milliseconds per simulation tick, Red Alert mod rule for the default profile; 40 ms gives 25 Hz

constants.name: Slowest timestep
constants.unit: milliseconds per simulation tick, Red Alert mod rule; 80 ms gives 12.5 Hz

constants.name: Fastest timestep
constants.unit: milliseconds per simulation tick, Red Alert mod rule; 20 ms gives 50 Hz

constants.name: Default order latency
constants.unit: network frames of the default profile, Red Alert mod rule, used in multiplayer; each network frame is 3 simulation ticks, so 9 ticks or 360 milliseconds at 25 Hz

constants.name: Network frame interval
constants.unit: simulation ticks per network frame, engine default session setting; 120 milliseconds at 25 Hz

cards.name: Terrain speed modifiers
cards.summary: Terrain scales each unit's base speed with a percentage table, and roads make tracked units faster than clear ground. Values are Red Alert mod rules for the foot and tracked locomotors.
cards.behavior: Each locomotor defines a speed percentage per terrain type. The unit's base speed is multiplied by the active terrain percentage and by any trait speed modifiers. Missing terrain entries are impassable and receive an unreachable path cost. Pathfinding uses the same table to prefer faster ground. Foot units slow down on rough ground and gain a modest bonus on roads. Tracked units keep most of their speed on rough ground and gain a larger road bonus.

constants.name: Foot speed on clear ground
constants.unit: percent of base speed, read each simulation tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Foot speed on rough ground
constants.unit: percent of base speed, read each simulation tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Foot speed on roads
constants.unit: percent of base speed, read each simulation tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Tracked speed on rough ground
constants.unit: percent of base speed, read each simulation tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Tracked speed on roads
constants.unit: percent of base speed, read each simulation tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Pathing cost numerator
constants.unit: cost units; path cost per cell is this number divided by the terrain speed percentage (integer division) unless the rules give an explicit cost; computed once when rules load, no timestep

cards.name: Ground move progress and turning
cards.summary: Ground units advance along a path by their current speed each tick and rotate the body toward the next cell.
cards.behavior: A move activity stores the current cell and the next cell, then blends position between their centers. On each tick the unit adds its terrain-adjusted speed to a progress value expressed in world distance units. When progress reaches the segment length, the unit snaps to the next cell and starts the next segment. The body follows the path with a limited turn rate. A near reversal (turn angle between 135 and 225 degrees) is handled by turning in place first, while other direction changes produce a curved trajectory. The carryover rule lets a unit take at most one full speed step in a tick.

constants.name: Dog ground speed
constants.unit: world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), Red Alert mod rule for the dog actor, before terrain percentage, at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Grenadier ground speed
constants.unit: world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), Red Alert mod rule for the grenadier actor, before terrain percentage, at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Default body turn rate
constants.unit: angle units per tick (1024 units per full turn), engine default at the default 25 Hz; Red Alert infantry keep it and the vehicle base rule sets 20

constants.name: Tight U-turn lower angle
constants.unit: angle units of turn angle between the current and next path direction (1024 per full turn); turn angles from 384 to 640 (135 to 225 degrees) are turned in place, other nonzero angles curve; checked once per path segment

constants.name: Tight U-turn upper angle
constants.unit: angle units of turn angle between the current and next path direction (1024 per full turn); turn angles from 384 to 640 (135 to 225 degrees) are turned in place, other nonzero angles curve; checked once per path segment

constants.name: World distance units per cell
constants.unit: world distance units per cell, used as the movement and combat distance scale at the default 25 Hz

cards.name: Blocked movement and repathing
cards.summary: A moving unit waits for a blocker, nudges it when possible, and may reverse or repath after the wait expires.
cards.behavior: When the next cell is occupied, the mover asks the blocker to move and waits for the locomotor wait average, which is 40 ticks or about 1.6 seconds at the default rate. If the blocker cannot move at all, the mover repaths at once. When the wait expires, the mover recalculates a path unless the blockers are already leaving. If no path exists and the mover itself blocks another unit, it steps aside. A mover may also back up instead of turning around, but only when its Mobile trait enables reversing; that option is off by default and no Red Alert actor rule turns it on. Reversing is limited by a 40-tick duration and fewer than 15 remaining path cells.

constants.name: Blocker wait
constants.unit: simulation ticks counted down once per tick at the default 25 Hz, about 1.6 seconds; engine default locomotor value, kept by the Red Alert rules

constants.name: Backward duration
constants.unit: simulation ticks since the move began, at the default 25 Hz; engine default, only used when reversing is enabled (default off)

constants.name: Maximum backward path
constants.unit: cells; reversing needs fewer remaining path cells than this, tested when a path segment starts; engine default, only used when reversing is enabled

constants.name: Backward turn threshold
constants.unit: angle units (1024 per full turn); reversing is chosen when the first facing differs from the current facing by more than 256 (90 degrees), tested when a path segment starts

constants.name: Backward facing offset
constants.unit: angle units (half turn, 180 degrees) added to the facing to drive in reverse, set when a path segment starts

cards.name: Weighted hierarchical A-star
cards.summary: OpenRA uses weighted A-star over a terrain-cost grid, sped up by a coarse abstract graph and a short-range shortcut.
cards.behavior: The pathfinder treats each cell as a node with a movement cost derived from terrain speed. It explores the map with A-star and a diagonal-distance heuristic. It accepts paths up to 25 percent longer than optimal to reduce search work. For most searches it runs a guided bidirectional search over an abstract graph whose nodes are 10-by-10 cell regions. Very short routes skip the abstract graph and search a small local grid with the optimal-weight heuristic. A move between adjacent cells is returned without a search.

constants.name: Default heuristic weight
constants.unit: percent of the optimal heuristic, engine default; the pathfinder floors the setting at 100; no timestep

constants.name: Local heuristic weight
constants.unit: percent of the optimal heuristic, used for short local path searches at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Abstract grid size
constants.unit: cells per abstract grid side, rebuilt when terrain costs change at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Close-grid distance
constants.unit: abstract grid widths, used as the short-route threshold at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Adjacent-cell squared distance
constants.unit: squared cell distance, strict upper bound: orthogonal (1) and diagonal (2) neighbors skip the search; checked per path request, no timestep

cards.name: Edge and key scrolling
cards.summary: The camera scrolls when the pointer reaches a five-pixel border, with a 30-pixel step per 25 milliseconds of frame time, applied every rendered frame.
cards.behavior: Edge scrolling is enabled by default. The pointer must enter the outer five pixels of the window to start scrolling. The scroll direction is a unit vector combined from all active edges and keys. Each rendered frame the camera scrolls by the step setting times the elapsed milliseconds divided by 25, with the elapsed time capped at 25 milliseconds, so a long frame cannot produce a large jump and frame times above 25 ms slow the scroll. At the full cap that is 30 pixels per 25 ms, or 1200 pixels per second. The source comment names a 40 millisecond interval, but the code divides by 25. The step is divided by the current zoom and the center is clamped to the map bounds. Camera scrolling runs once per rendered frame, not on the 25 Hz world tick.

constants.name: Edge scroll margin
constants.unit: screen pixels from each window edge, engine default player setting, tested every rendered frame

constants.name: Edge scroll step
constants.unit: screen pixels per 25 ms of frame time (30 px per 25 ms at full cap), engine default player setting, applied every rendered frame and divided by zoom

constants.name: Joystick scroll rate factor
constants.unit: multiplier on the scroll step setting per pixel of pointer drag offset, applied every rendered frame with no time scaling

constants.name: Elapsed time cap
constants.unit: milliseconds of wall-clock time since the last scroll update, also the divisor of the step formula; applied every rendered frame

constants.name: Minimum scroll vector length
constants.unit: dimensionless floor on the summed direction vector length before normalizing; no timestep

cards.name: Exponential zoom
cards.summary: Zoom is an exponential multiplier whose range comes from the window size and viewport setting, with the maximum at twice the minimum, and a wheel step of 0.04 per notch.
cards.behavior: The viewport stores zoom as a multiplier on native resolution. A wheel step adds or subtracts 0.04 per unit of wheel delta to an exponent, so equal forward and backward steps have equal visual effect, and no modifier key is required by default. The result is clamped between the minimum and maximum zoom. The minimum comes from the window height and the viewport-distance setting; the property initial values of one and two are replaced at setup. The maximum is the smaller of twice the minimum and the value that keeps at least 240 world pixels of height visible. Zooming around the cursor keeps the world point under the pointer fixed by adjusting the center before the map clamp. A larger zoom value shows a smaller world area.

constants.name: Maximum zoom ratio
constants.unit: ratio of maximum zoom to minimum zoom (dimensionless), engine default of the viewport size rules, which Red Alert does not override; set when the viewport is set up

constants.name: Maximum zoom height floor
constants.unit: world pixels of visible window height at maximum zoom, engine default; caps the maximum zoom; set when the viewport is set up

constants.name: Wheel zoom speed
constants.unit: exponent increment per unit of wheel delta, engine default player setting, applied on wheel input events (not on the 25 Hz world tick)

cards.name: Fixed-wing flight and turn radius
cards.summary: Fixed-wing aircraft fly forward at a constant speed and turn toward a target in a wide circle.
cards.behavior: An aircraft moves along its facing by its flight speed each tick. Steering changes facing at a limited rate, and the resulting motion follows a circular arc rather than a sharp corner. The turn radius is derived from speed divided by turn rate and scaled by 180, so fast or slow-turning aircraft need wide turns. A small facing deadzone prevents visual jitter near the target bearing. Height changes are capped by a maximum pitch while the aircraft moves horizontally. If the target lies inside the current turn circle, the aircraft keeps its heading and flies around instead of reversing.

constants.name: U2 cruise speed
constants.unit: world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), Red Alert mod rule for the U2 spy plane, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: U2 turn rate
constants.unit: angle units per tick (1024 units per full turn), Red Alert mod rule for the U2 spy plane, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: U2 cruise altitude
constants.unit: world distance units above terrain (1024 units per cell), Red Alert mod rule for the U2 spy plane, held per tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: U2 maximum pitch
constants.unit: angle units of pitch cap (1024 units per full turn), Red Alert mod rule for the U2 spy plane, checked per simulation tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Turn deadzone
constants.unit: angle units (1024 per full turn) of facing error ignored; engine default, tested per tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Turn radius scale
constants.unit: dimensionless factor: turn radius in world units is 180 times speed (units per tick) divided by turn rate (angle units per tick); 1024 divided by two pi is about 163, rounded up for leeway; evaluated per tick at the default 25 Hz

cards.name: Vertical takeoff and landing
cards.summary: Aircraft climb vertically when hovering or VTOL, search nearby cells for a landing spot, and retry airports on an interval.
cards.behavior: Aircraft treat themselves as airborne above a minimum altitude and climb toward cruise altitude. VTOL and hovering aircraft change altitude at a fixed vertical speed while keeping horizontal position. Landing searches outward up to five cells when the requested cell is blocked, then approaches the selected cell and descends. The default cruise altitude is 1280 world distance units, while the Red Alert transport helicopter overrides the default vertical speed of 43 units per tick with 58. An aircraft waiting for a resupply airport rechecks availability every 150 ticks.

constants.name: Transport helicopter speed
constants.unit: world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), Red Alert mod rule for the transport helicopter, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Transport helicopter climb rate
constants.unit: world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), written as 0c58 in the Red Alert mod rule for the transport helicopter, applied to vertical-only moves at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Default cruise altitude
constants.unit: world distance units above terrain (1024 units per cell), engine default, held per tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Default vertical speed
constants.unit: world distance units per tick, engine default for vertical take-off, landing and hovering to cruise altitude, at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Minimum airborne altitude
constants.unit: world distance units above terrain, checked per simulation tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Landing search radius
constants.unit: cells around the requested landing cell, searched per landing attempt at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Airport recheck interval
constants.unit: simulation ticks at the default 25 Hz, equal to 6 seconds

cards.name: Turret tracking
cards.summary: Turreted vehicles rotate their turret toward the target at a fixed rate and recenter after a delay.
cards.behavior: A turret has its own local facing. When a target is set, the turret rotates toward the target direction at its turn speed until the facing matches. The body can keep moving while the turret tracks. When the turret stops aiming, a realignment delay of 40 ticks must pass before it returns to its initial facing. The Red Alert light tank uses a turret turn rate of 28 angle units per tick, while the medium and heavy tanks use 20.

constants.name: Light tank turret turn rate
constants.unit: angle units per tick (1024 units per full turn), Red Alert mod rule, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Medium tank turret turn rate
constants.unit: angle units per tick (1024 units per full turn), Red Alert mod rule, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Heavy tank turret turn rate
constants.unit: angle units per tick (1024 units per full turn), Red Alert mod rule, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Default turret turn rate
constants.unit: angle units per tick (1024 units per full turn), engine default, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Turret realign delay
constants.unit: simulation ticks without aiming at the default 25 Hz, equal to 1.6 seconds; engine default, minus one turns realignment off

cards.name: Burst fire and reload
cards.summary: Weapons fire a fixed burst, pause between shots, then wait a reload delay before the next burst.
cards.behavior: Each weapon has a burst count. After each shot the armament sets a countdown: the burst delay while shots remain in the burst, or the reload delay after the last shot (reload modifiers apply, with a floor of one tick). The countdown drops by one per tick and the weapon can fire again only at zero. Recoil is applied on firing and recovers a fixed amount each tick. In the Red Alert rules the 105mm cannon fires two shots per burst with a 70-tick reload, and the heavy tank mounting it recovers 38 recoil units per tick, while the default armament recovery is 9 units per tick.

constants.name: Cannon reload delay
constants.unit: simulation ticks between bursts at the default 25 Hz, equal to 2 seconds; Red Alert weapon rule for the shared cannon base

constants.name: 105mm reload delay
constants.unit: simulation ticks between bursts at the default 25 Hz, equal to 2.8 seconds; Red Alert weapon rule

constants.name: 105mm burst size
constants.unit: shots per burst, separated by the burst delay; Red Alert weapon rule

constants.name: Default burst delay
constants.unit: simulation ticks between shots inside a burst at the default 25 Hz, equal to 200 milliseconds; engine default

constants.name: Turret recoil recovery
constants.unit: world distance units of recoil recovered per tick at the default 25 Hz; Red Alert rule for the heavy tank armament

constants.name: Default recoil recovery
constants.unit: world distance units of recoil recovered per tick at the default 25 Hz; engine default

constants.name: Air target threshold
constants.unit: world distance units above terrain; engine default altitude above which a non-actor target counts as air; checked per target test

cards.name: Bullet ballistics
cards.summary: Bullets travel in a straight line or parabolic arc at a fixed world speed and can be made inaccurate or bouncy.
cards.behavior: A bullet computes its flight length from the distance to the impact point divided by its speed, with a one-tick minimum. Each tick it moves along a quadratic curve between source and target, which gives artillery a visible arc when a launch angle is set. Inaccuracy offsets the target with a random sample before the path is built. A bounce count lets the projectile rebound from the ground, and each bounce shortens the range by a percentage. The projectile explodes when the flight length is reached or when it hits a blocking actor.

constants.name: Cannon bullet speed
constants.unit: world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), Red Alert weapon rule for the shared cannon base, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Artillery launch angle
constants.unit: angle units (1024 per full turn, about 22 degrees), Red Alert weapon rule, set once at projectile creation

constants.name: Artillery inaccuracy
constants.unit: written as 1 cell plus 938 subunits, which is 1962 world distance units of maximum random offset; Red Alert weapon rule, sampled once at projectile creation

constants.name: Grenade speed
constants.unit: world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), Red Alert weapon rule for the grenadier, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Grenade inaccuracy
constants.unit: world distance units of maximum random offset, Red Alert weapon rule, sampled once at projectile creation

constants.name: Default bullet speed
constants.unit: world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), engine default, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Bounce range modifier
constants.unit: percent of the previous bounce distance used for the next bounce, engine default; bouncing is off unless a weapon sets a bounce count above its default of 0

constants.name: Minimum flight duration
constants.unit: simulation tick at the default 25 Hz, floor on flight length (distance divided by speed, integer division)

cards.name: Missile homing
cards.summary: Missiles use freefall then homing flight, with limited turn rates, a proximity fuse, and fuel range.
cards.behavior: A missile starts unarmed and can explode only after its arming delay. Before propulsion activates it falls under gravity. After activation it accelerates to its maximum speed and turns horizontally and vertically toward a predicted target position. A lock-on probability controls whether the guidance follows the target. If it passes its range limit, it switches back to freefall and explodes when empty. It also explodes when it comes within the proximity radius, which is 298 units by default. The anti-ground missile reaches 213 units per tick, arms after two ticks, and turns at 20 angle units per tick.

constants.name: Anti-ground missile speed
constants.unit: Red Alert weapon rule; world distance units per tick (1024 units per cell), applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Anti-ground missile arming delay
constants.unit: Red Alert weapon rule; simulation ticks at the default 25 Hz, equal to 80 milliseconds; a missile that explodes on or before this tick deals no damage

constants.name: Anti-ground missile turn rate
constants.unit: Red Alert weapon rule; angle units per tick (1024 units per full turn), applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Anti-ground missile range limit
constants.unit: Red Alert weapon rule; 6 cells, which is 6144 world distance units of path flown before fuel runs out, checked per tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Default missile gravity
constants.unit: world distance units per tick squared during freefall, engine default, applied at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Default proximity fuse radius
constants.unit: world distance units, engine default, checked per simulation tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Default cruise altitude
constants.unit: world distance units above terrain (1024 units per cell), engine default, held per tick at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Lock-on probability
constants.unit: percent chance per missile launch, engine default

cards.name: Armor-class damage scaling
cards.summary: Damage is scaled by armor type percentages, so the same shell does different damage to different targets.
cards.behavior: A warhead carries raw damage and a table of percentages per armor class. When a hit lands, the engine multiplies raw damage by the percentage of every matching armor trait on the target and by any damage modifiers. If the table is empty, the multiplier is 100 percent. Damage falls off with distance from the impact in steps of the spread value, by default to 100, 37, 14, 5 and 0 percent at 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 steps. The Red Alert cannon warhead deals 4000 raw damage with a 128-unit step and applies 30 percent against unarmored targets, 75 percent against wood and light armor, and 50 percent against concrete. The 90mm shell applies 115 percent against heavy armor.

constants.name: Cannon raw damage
constants.unit: hit points per warhead impact at the impact center, Red Alert weapon rule, applied instantly at the default 25 Hz

constants.name: Cannon damage spread
constants.unit: world distance units between damage falloff steps, Red Alert weapon rule, evaluated per hit

constants.name: Default falloff steps
constants.unit: percent of damage at 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4 spread steps from the impact, engine default for the spread damage warhead, evaluated per hit

constants.name: Damage versus unarmored
constants.unit: percent of raw damage per hit, Red Alert weapon rule

constants.name: Damage versus wood armor
constants.unit: percent of raw damage per hit, Red Alert weapon rule

constants.name: Damage versus light armor
constants.unit: percent of raw damage per hit, Red Alert weapon rule

constants.name: Damage versus concrete armor
constants.unit: percent of raw damage per hit, Red Alert weapon rule

constants.name: 90mm damage versus heavy armor
constants.unit: percent of raw damage per hit, Red Alert weapon rule

constants.name: Default damage percentage
constants.unit: percent of raw damage per hit when the armor table is empty, engine default

cards.name: Health bands and death
cards.summary: Health tracks four damage bands and removes the actor when hit points reach zero.
cards.behavior: An actor stores current and maximum hit points. The damage state is undamaged at full health, light above 75 percent but below full, medium below 75 percent, heavy below 50 percent, and critical below 25 percent. Death occurs at zero, and overkill damage is not counted again. A scenario can spawn an actor at a percentage of its maximum health. The medium tank has 46000 hit points, so its heavy band starts below 23000 and its critical band starts below 11500.

constants.name: Medium tank hit points
constants.unit: hit points at full health, Red Alert mod rule for the medium tank

constants.name: Critical band threshold
constants.unit: percent of maximum hit points; the band applies strictly below this value; engine rule, checked on each damage event

constants.name: Heavy band threshold
constants.unit: percent of maximum hit points; the band applies strictly below this value; engine rule, checked on each damage event

constants.name: Medium band threshold
constants.unit: percent of maximum hit points; the band applies strictly below this value; engine rule, checked on each damage event

constants.name: Health init scale
constants.unit: percent divisor: a spawn health value is a percent of maximum hit points, applied at actor creation

constants.name: Minimum hit points
constants.unit: hit points; a configured maximum of zero or less becomes this value at actor creation
